data.final_week_advice: Use the remaining time to take a full-length timed practice test, then review all incorrect answers in detail, focusing on the units that were most challenging.
data.summary: This 4‑week plan covers every AP Chemistry unit with focused, concrete tasks and a single live class in week 4. Each week uses the full 5 hours, balancing new content, practice, and review, and the final week is a mixed‑review session to solidify concepts before the exam.

weeks.focus: Build a strong foundation in atomic structure and basic properties.
tasks: Read the textbook section on 1.1 and write a 200‑word summary of moles and molar mass.
Do 10 practice problems on converting grams to moles, then check answers with the scoring guide.
Watch the recorded lecture on 1.5 and diagram the electron configuration of sodium.
Solve 5 multiple‑choice questions on periodic trends (1.7) and explain each answer choice.

weeks.focus: Explore compound structure, bonding, and basic reaction representations.
tasks: Create flashcards for ionic, covalent, and metallic bonds (2.1).
Draw Lewis structures for 5 molecules (2.5) and label formal charges.
Write out the balanced equation for the reaction of HCl with NaOH and then convert it to a net ionic equation (4.3).
Answer 8 practice questions on Lewis diagrams and reaction representations, marking each with the rubric.
Plot a rate vs. concentration graph for a first‑order reaction (5.1).
Calculate ΔH for the combustion of methane using Hess’s law (6.1).
Sketch an energy diagram for the reaction and label activation energy (6.2).
Complete 6 timed practice problems on rate laws and heat transfer, recording time taken.

weeks.focus: Integrate equilibrium concepts and review all units with a live class.
tasks: After class, solve 4 equilibrium constant problems (7.3).
Review 1.2 by interpreting a mass‑spectrometry spectrum for a pure element.
Do a stoichiometry worksheet (4.5) involving a multi‑step reaction.
Practice 5 rate‑law questions (5.2) and compare answers with the scoring guide.
